solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Didn’t drink six-pack and exercised, right away (9)

indicators.note: something sent away is no longer there, so R is taken out of TRAINED

blocks.note: a six-pack is a set of well-defined abdominal muscles, the abs
R = right; it is removed, leaving TAINED

annotation.surface: A fitness fanatic stays off the booze, works out and hits the gym.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma splits the surface's list of virtues but not the wordplay: 'right away' is an instruction on 'exercised', not a separate item.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a narrowed sense: to abstain is to refrain, most often from alcohol.

entries.clue: Fabulous writer regularly sampling mater’s soup (5)

indicators.note: sampling at regular intervals takes every second letter

annotation.surface: A writer tastes his mother's soup.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' looks like praise but is literal: this writer's stock in trade was fables.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal reading of 'fabulous', of fables: Aesop is the ancient Greek teller of the animal fables.

entries.clue: Snake exhausted after eating wings of eider (7)

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside, so SPENT takes ER inside
a bird's wings are at its sides, so a word's wings are its outer letters

annotation.surface: A snake, tired out after swallowing a duck.
annotation.walkthrough: An eider is a sea duck; the snake-eats-bird picture is apt, but only the duck's edges are swallowed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: serpent is the older, literary word for snake.

entries.clue: Famous Greek agreed to stop god of war (10)

indicators.note: a stopper goes inside a bottle's neck, so CHIMED goes inside ARES

blocks.note: to chime with is to agree with
Ares is the Greek god of war

annotation.surface: A renowned Greek agrees to halt the war god.
annotation.walkthrough: The Greek setting makes Ares the natural god to reach for, and the famous Greek is the one of the bath and 'Eureka!'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Archimedes, mathematician of Syracuse, is one of the best-known ancient Greeks.

entries.clue: What suggests self-confidence of acrobat group? (5)

blocks.note: an acrobat working without a safety net is showing confidence; split the answer 2+3
a set of nine players, like a trio or quartet

annotation.surface: A question about what shows a troupe of acrobats is sure of itself.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the answer as NO NET: no safety net means a confident acrobat. 'Acrobat group' reads as one phrase, a troupe, but 'group' alone is the second definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: NO NET is the daredevil's sign of confidence, and a nonet is a group of nine musicians.

entries.clue: Follow mountain pass, initially left and right, in special clothing (3,6)

indicators.note: at the start of each word, so take the first letters of 'left and right'

blocks.note: to dog someone is to follow them
a col is a pass between peaks
the initials of Left And Right

annotation.surface: Directions for a hiker: take the pass, turn left and right, wearing proper gear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Initially' seems to apply only to 'left', but it covers all three words, including 'and'.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint at vocation: a dog collar is the white clerical collar, clothing special to the clergy.

entries.clue: Plant tax collecting rupees (5)

indicators.note: a collector gathers things into its keeping, so CESS gathers R inside it

blocks.note: a cess is a tax or levy
R is the abbreviation for rupees

annotation.surface: A plant tax is levied in rupees.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' could be a verb or a factory in the surface; it is the green kind, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: cress, the peppery salad sprout, is one kind of plant.

entries.clue: Dog food (4)

blocks.note: a fluffy Chinese breed with a blue-black tongue
slang for grub, from pidgin English

annotation.surface: A label on a tin of pet food.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words read as one phrase, dog food, but each is a separate definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: the chow chow is a dog breed, and chow is slang for food.

entries.clue: Back the last nag leaving the start (7)

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, and it leaves: H is dropped from HORSE

blocks.note: a nag is an old horse; lose the first letter to leave ORSE

annotation.surface: A racegoer backs the tail-ender just as it leaves the starting gate.
annotation.walkthrough: Racing words, 'back', 'nag', 'start', all point to a bet; 'Back' is the definition, meaning support.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to endorse a candidate or product is to back it.

entries.clue: Veronica went very fast, stuck with ultimately large fine (9)

indicators.note: something stuck with a thing is lodged in it, so E is lodged inside SPED
at the end, so take the last letter of 'large'

annotation.surface: A woman called Veronica drove too fast and got hit with a big fine.
annotation.walkthrough: Veronica reads as a speeding driver, but it is a botanical genus name.
annotation.definitionFit: A botanical name: Veronica is the Latin genus of speedwell, a small blue-flowered plant.

entries.clue: Moor Hospital hosts event (7)

indicators.note: a host has guests inside the house, so SAN holds RACE

blocks.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
a race is an event at a sports meeting

annotation.surface: A hospital puts on a fundraising event, with Moor at the head of the list.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moor' looks like open heathland; it is a person, the medieval Muslim of North Africa and Spain.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical synonym: medieval Europeans called Muslims Saracens and, in Spain and North Africa, Moors.

entries.clue: Dire ego failed NE resident (7)

indicators.note: something that has failed has broken down, so the letters break apart and are rebuilt

annotation.surface: A northerner's terrible self-image lets them down.
annotation.walkthrough: NE is north-east England, the area around Newcastle upon Tyne.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional nickname: a Geordie is a native of Tyneside in England's north-east.

entries.clue: Fancy ignoring the French forecast (10)

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so LE goes from PREDILECTION

blocks.note: a predilection is a fancy, a liking
le is French for 'the'; it is removed

annotation.surface: A fancy forecast that snubs the French.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' is a noun here, a liking, not the adjective the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a forecast is a prediction of what is to come.

entries.clue: Poke with tip of pointed stick (4)

indicators.note: the tip is the leading end, so take the first letter of 'pointed'

annotation.surface: Poke something with the sharp end of a stick.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a plain description of what the answer means, so the answer sits in the picture too.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to poke and to prod are the same jab.

entries.clue: Tormented soul; obtain forgiveness! (10)

indicators.note: to torment once meant to twist or wrench, so the letters are twisted about

annotation.surface: A cry to a tortured soul: go and get yourself forgiven!
annotation.walkthrough: 'Obtain' looks like an instruction in the surface but is fodder; the definition is only the last word.
annotation.definitionFit: A religious sense: absolution is a priest's formal forgiveness of sins.

entries.clue: Ignited high explosive fluid (5)

blocks.note: HE is the abbreviation for high explosive

annotation.surface: A volatile explosive liquid was set alight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fluid' reads as a noun, a liquid; it is the adjective, graceful in movement.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative synonym: fluid movement is smooth and supple, which is what lithe describes.

entries.clue: Part of Listener puzzle? (9)

blocks.note: a listener is anyone hearing; the part meant is the inner ear
a maze, a puzzle to find the way through

annotation.surface: A question about one element of a Listener crossword.
annotation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famously hard crossword published with The Times, so 'Listener puzzle' reads as one thing; here a listener is just someone hearing, and the inner ear is called the labyrinth.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: the inner ear's winding canals are the labyrinth, and a labyrinth is a maze.

entries.clue: Receive verbal lashing after going round pinching guidance for players (4,5)

indicators.note: turning round means facing back, so the letters are read backwards
to pinch is to steal a bit, so the answer is lifted from inside the words

annotation.surface: Someone takes a telling-off after being caught stealing on their rounds.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs backwards through the first three words, with 'verbal' there whole. 'Players' are musicians, not actors or sportsmen.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical term: alla breve on a score tells players to count two minim beats to the bar.

entries.clue: Pseudoscientist saving wife from crazed Salem witch (9)

indicators.note: saving can mean except, so W is left out
the W comes away from the fodder
something crazed is cracked all over, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife; it is removed, leaving SALEMITCH

annotation.surface: A quack rescues his wife from a mad Salem witch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saving' seems to mean rescuing; here it means except, so the W is taken out.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: alchemy, turning base metal into gold, is the classic pseudoscience.

entries.clue: Batter tailless fish where cooks train? (6,3)

indicators.note: a word's tail is its last letter, so CARP loses its P

blocks.note: a carp is a freshwater fish; without its tail it is CAR

annotation.surface: A cookery school coats a fish in batter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Batter' is the cook's mix in the surface; it is the verb, to pound. The definition reads train as a noun, not the verb of cooks in training.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: the buffet car is the carriage on a train where food is cooked and served.

entries.clue: Article on Pacific island country featured in excellent publication (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, A sits on top of NZ
something featured in a show appears within it, so ANZ appears inside FINE

annotation.surface: A glowing magazine piece about a Pacific nation.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes the article a piece of writing; it is the grammatical article.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a fanzine, a fan-made amateur magazine, is one kind of publication.

entries.clue: Dyke-builder left rubbish (5)

blocks.note: Offa, king of Mercia, gave his name to the dyke along the Welsh border

annotation.surface: The man who built the dyke left a heap of rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: Offa's Dyke is an eighth-century earthwork running roughly along the England–Wales border.
annotation.definitionFit: An older sense: offal, literally what falls off, also means refuse or waste.

entries.clue: More hazy character of Verne’s work? That’s right (7)

blocks.note: Phileas Fogg, hero of Around the World in Eighty Days

annotation.surface: A question about a vague figure in Jules Verne, then a confirmation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That's right' reads as a reply; the first word is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: fog makes things hazy, so foggier is more hazy.

entries.clue: Offensive practical joke deposes leader (4)

indicators.note: deposing a leader removes whoever is at the top, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: a prank is a practical joke; drop the P

annotation.surface: A tasteless prank topples the boss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' reads as the adjective describing the joke; it is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rank means foul or offensive, especially of a smell.

entries.clue: Patty sent back food following complaint, beginning to experience runs (10)

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so GRUB is read in reverse
coming after, so the reversed food goes after the complaint
the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: grub = food; sent back it reads BURG

annotation.surface: Patty sends her meal back with a complaint, then gets an upset stomach.
annotation.walkthrough: Patty reads as a diner's name; it is the definition, the minced-meat disc. 'Runs' in the surface is diarrhoea, but in the wordplay it is the cricket-scoring abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a patty is a flat cake of minced meat, and the beefburger is the commonest one.

entries.clue: French ref’s unfair person (5)

blocks.note: ump, short for umpire, is a ref

annotation.surface: A French referee is biased.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unfair' suggests a biased ref, but here it means not fair to look at: plain.
annotation.definitionFit: A play on fair as beautiful: a frump is a dowdy, unattractive woman, someone 'un-fair'.

entries.clue: Material artist over there (5)

blocks.note: yon is archaic for over there

annotation.surface: Pointing out some cloth for a painter across the room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Material' could be an artist's subject matter; it is fabric.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: material means fabric, and rayon is one, made from cellulose.

entries.clue: Indian state home to unknown artist (4)

indicators.note: a place that is home to something holds it within, so GOA houses Y

blocks.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast

annotation.surface: An Indian state is home to an obscure painter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unknown' reads as obscure, describing the artist; it is the algebraic letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Francisco Goya was a Spanish painter.

entries.clue: Capital city’s new appearance and charm (7)

blocks.note: an air is a manner or appearance
obi (obeah) is a West Indian charm or fetish

annotation.surface: A capital has a fresh look and much charm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charm' reads as appeal; here it is a magical object.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Nairobi is one capital city, that of Kenya.

entries.clue: Pointlessness when cancelling key public service (7)

indicators.note: to cancel is to strike out, so F is struck out of FUTILITY

blocks.note: F is a musical key; it is removed

annotation.surface: A complaint that a public service is useless once it cuts its key element.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' means important in the surface; it is a musical key, one of A to G.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialised sense: a utility is a public service such as water, gas or electricity supply.

entries.clue: Hard currency area? One has to laugh (5)

annotation.surface: An economist jokes about a strong-currency zone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hard currency area' reads as one economic phrase; it splits into three pieces. 'One has to laugh' sounds like a shrug but is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: the spotted hyena is famous for its cackling 'laugh', so it is one that has to laugh.

entries.clue: Poor Pandit Nehru, eh, missing a game of cricket (3-3-3)

indicators.note: in poor shape, so the letters are in a mess
what is missing is gone, so EH is taken from the fodder

annotation.surface: Pity poor Nehru, sitting out a cricket match.
annotation.walkthrough: Pandit Nehru was India's first prime minister.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: tip-and-run is an informal cricket game in which the batter must run whenever bat touches ball.
